label: UniFi Dream Wall
description: UniFi Dream Wall (UDW) - 17x 1G RJ45 LAN (4 PoE++ / 4 PoE+ / 4 PoE) + 1x 2.5G RJ45 WAN, 2x 10G SFP+ (10G/1G; one LAN and one WAN by default), and up to 8 ports configurable as WAN. WiFi 6; 112 W max excluding PoE output (532 W with the 420 W PoE budget).
notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udw (HTTP 200, 704,702 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = Universal AC input 100-240V AC, 7A Max., 50/60 Hz"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so eth12 / eth13 / eth14 / eth15 / eth16 / eth17 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

WiFi: the Dream Wall carries an 802.11ax (WiFi 6) access point of its own, so the row can serve wireless clients instead of being a wired-only gateway. Source rows, identical on both Ubiquiti surfaces: https://dl.ui.com/ds/udw_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, 544,909 B, 3 pages, text layer reads "MIMO 2.4 GHz 2 x 2 / 5 GHz 4 x 4", "Throughput rate 2.4 GHz 300 Mbps / 5 GHz 2.4 Gbps", "WiFi standards 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax / WiFi 4/WiFi 5/WiFi 6") and https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udw (HTTP 200, 704,702 B, read 2026-11-19). Hence radio0 = 2.4 GHz at 300 Mbps (2x2) and radio1 = 5 GHz at 2.4 Gbps (4x4). Each radio declares `bands` because engine/media.js otherwise derives the band set from the rate alone, and a 2.4 Gbps 802.11ax radio would be credited with a 6 GHz band the chassis does not have. Ubiquiti's own device fingerprint lists ACCESS_POINT among the UDW's deviceCapabilities (https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json, sku UDW, sysid ea2a).

WAN side, from the same two surfaces (read 2026-11-20). The datasheet text layer says "Networking interface (17) LAN: GbE RJ45 ports / (1) WAN: 2.5 GbE RJ45 port" and "SFP+ interface (1) LAN: 10G SFP+ port / (1) WAN: 10G SFP+ port" (https://dl.ui.com/ds/udw_ds.pdf, 200, 544,909 B, 3 pp); the tech-spec table adds "Max. WAN Port Count 8", "Default WAN Ports (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45 / (1) 10G SFP+" and "Port Layout ... 2.5 GbE RJ45 1 (2.5G/1G/100M)" (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udw, 200, 704,702 B). The row had shipped all eighteen copper ports as interchangeable eth0-eth17 with no WAN role, so a lab could not cable `ip nat outside` to the uplink Ubiquiti designates, and the 2.5G port was indistinguishable from the 1G LAN bank. eth17 is therefore wan1 with role "wan"; the two cages declare dualRole ["wan","lan"] because the datasheet prints one LAN and one WAN cage without numbering them, and because the vendor's own 8-WAN ceiling means port role is configuration, not wiring. The seventeen 1G LAN ports keep their names.
